## **5.2 \- GUI Programming** {#5.2---gui-programming}

### **5.2.1 \- Database Layer Programming** {#5.2.1---database-layer-programming}

The database layer consists of all server-side logic executed directly in MariaDB. This layer includes stored procedures, views, and triggers that support our GUI by enforcing business rules, simplifying queries, and maintaining data integrity. Each component below describes its purpose, where it is used in the application, and which user groups it serves.

#### **5.2.1.1 Stored Procedures** {#5.2.1.1-stored-procedures}

1. **register\_user**

This procedure validates and inserts new users into the ‘users’ table. It checks for missing fields, enforces valid roles (admin, player, guest), and prevents duplicate emails before creating the account. If validation passes, the user is inserted, and a confirmation message is returned. 

This procedure is invoked by register.php. When a guest submits the registration form, the PHP script executes the SQL command CALL register\_user(...). The procedure returns a success or error message (e.g., "Email already exists"), which the GUI displays to the user. This serves Guests and Players (registering an account). 

2. **delete\_tournament**

Safely deletes a tournament only if it is not active and contains no active matchups. The procedure checks tournament existence, ensures it is not currently running, removes all related votes, matchups, and entries, and finally deletes the tournament record. 

This is invoked by delete\_tournament.php, which is triggered when a user clicks the "Delete" button on the Profile Dashboard (for tournament owners) or the Admin Panel (for Admins). The PHP script passes the Tournament ID and the User’s Role to the procedure to enforce permission checks. The user groups served with this procedure would be Admins (full deletion rights) and Players (limited use — can only delete their own tournaments before they start). 

3. **get\_tournament\_stats**

Generates a complete statistical report for a tournament. This includes tournament overview, total entries, matchups, votes, and a unique voter count. It also produces the average votes per matchup,the top 5 most popular entries, and the vote distribution by round into a single procedure call, avoiding the need for multiple expensive queries from the client. This data powers the GUI’s tournament statistics page. 

This is used in statistics.php, the admin dashboard, and player-created tournament insights. The user groups served would be Players (viewing stats of tournaments they created or participated in) and Admins. 

#### ***5.2.1.2*** **Views** {#5.2.1.2-views}

1. **active\_matchups\_with\_votes**

Provides a consolidated view of all active matchups, including entry names and images, vote counts for each entry, total votes, and round number and closing times. 

This is used in the voting and results page. The user groups served Players (viewing active matchups). 

2. **view\_tournament\_entries**

Simplifies retrieving all entries for a tournament with their names and images. Used to display tournament bracket contents, entry details, and statistics pages. 

This is used in bracket renderin,g and the statistics display in statistics.ph,p displaying the full set of entries (with images) for a specific tournament. The user groups served with this would be Guests, Players, and Admins.

3. **view\_active\_tournaments**

Returns all tournaments with status ‘Active’. This simplifies the main browsing query by pre-filtering the tournament status, making it easier for the GUI to show what users can vote in. 

Utilized by tournaments.php to render the "Active" and "Upcoming" tournament lists without requiring the frontend code to understand the underlying status logic.. This serves all user groups. 

#### ***5.2.1.3 Triggers*** {#5.2.1.3-triggers}

1. **trg\_entry\_same\_ins and trg\_entry\_same\_upd**

Prevents duplicate entry names within the same tournament. If a user attempts to insert or rename an entry to a name that already exists in that tournament, the trigger blocks the operation and returns an error. This ensures bracket integrity and avoids confusing matchups.

These triggers fire automatically during the execution of create\_tournament.php. If a user attempts to upload duplicate entries, the database raises an error, which the GUI catches and reports to the user. The user groups served would be Players (prevents accidental duplicate entries).

2. **trg\_matchup\_select\_winner**

Automatically calculates the winning entry whenever a matchup status changes to "Completed." It counts votes and applies a seed-based tie-breaker if votes are tied or zero, ensuring every completed matchup has a valid winner.

This trigger fires immediately when config.php executes the SQL command UPDATE matchup SET status='Completed'. By moving this logic to a trigger, we eliminated redundant PHP calculation loops. The user groups served would be all users/visitors(Guest, Player, Admin) who see the tournaments.

#### ***5.2.1. 4 New Programming Logic for Phase 5:*** {#5.2.1.-4-new-programming-logic-for-phase-5:}

***Stored Procedures***

1. **create\_tournament**

To support the GUI's ‘Create Tournament’ function, we created a new procedure that handles the initialization of a tournament record in a single step. It accepts the tournament entry data (title, description, start-time, end-time, user\_id) and returns the newly created tournament\_id.

Called by create\_tournament.php. The returned ID is immediately used by the PHP script to associate the 16 uploaded entry images with the correct tournament.

**Code used to create:**

| `DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS create_tournament; DELIMITER // CREATE PROCEDURE create_tournament(     IN p_title        VARCHAR(255),     IN p_description  TEXT,     IN p_start        DATE,     IN p_end          DATE,     IN p_user_id      INT ) BEGIN     DECLARE v_status VARCHAR(20);     -- Decide tournament status based on dates     IF p_start > CURDATE() THEN         SET v_status = 'Upcoming';     ELSEIF p_end IS NOT NULL AND p_end < CURDATE() THEN         SET v_status = 'Completed';     ELSE         SET v_status = 'Active';     END IF;     -- Insert the new tournament     INSERT INTO tournament (title, description, start_at, end_at, tourneystatus, user_id)     VALUES (p_title, p_description, p_start, p_end, v_status, p_user_id);     -- Return the new tournament_id as a result set     SELECT LAST_INSERT_ID() AS new_tournament_id; END // DELIMITER ;` |
| :---- |

### **5.2.2 \- Application Layer Programming** {#5.2.2---application-layer-programming}

The application layer is implemented in PHP, running on Apache on the university’s Artemis server. This layer serves as the bridge between the GUI (HTML/CSS/JavaScript) and the database layer (MariaDB). It manages establishing secure database connections, executing SQL queries, views, and stored procedures, and also handles authentication and session states. The application layer also enforces semantic constraints not guaranteed by the database, validates and sanitizes user inputs, and formats query results for display in the GUI. 

Below are the key examples of PHP code that implement this functionality.

#### **5.2.2.1 Database Connection (config.php)** {#5.2.2.1-database-connection-(config.php)}

All PHP files load a shared PDO connection through config.php where we centralize the PDO connection and instead of creating new connection in every single file we just make use of the static variable from the get\_pdo\_connection() function .

| `<?php define("DB_HOST", "localhost"); define("DB_NAME", "fantasytourney"); define("DB_USER", "jsoto2"); define("DB_PASS", "********"); function get_pdo_connection() {     $dsn = "mysql:host=" . DB_HOST . ";dbname=" . DB_NAME;     $pdo = new PDO($dsn, DB_USER, DB_PASS);     $pdo->setAttribute(PDO::ATTR_ERRMODE, PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION);     return $pdo; } ?>` |
| :---- |

This provides a secure, centralized database connection, enables prepared statements, and ensures consistent error handling across all PHP pages. 

#### **5.2.2.2 Executing a Stored Procedure (register\_user)** {#5.2.2.2-executing-a-stored-procedure-(register_user)}

Register.php calls the stored procedure using prepared statements:

| `$stmt = $db->prepare("CALL register_user(?, ?, ?, ?)"); $stmt->execute([$email, $password, $displayname, $role]); $result = $stmt->fetchAll(PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);` |
| :---- |

This sends form data to MariaDB, receives DB-generated success/error messages, and ensures proper parameter binding. 

#### **5.2.2.3 Deleting a Tournament via Stored Procedure (delete\_tournament.php)** {#5.2.2.3-deleting-a-tournament-via-stored-procedure-(delete_tournament.php)}

Allows admins to delete tournaments while relying on the stored procedure to enforce rules (no deletion of active tournaments, safe cascading deletes).

| `$tournament_id = $_POST['tournament_id']; $stmt = $db->prepare("CALL delete_tournament(?)"); $stmt->execute([$tournament_id]); $message = $stmt->fetchColumn();  echo "<p>$message</p>";` |
| :---- |

#### **5.2.2.4 Using a View to Fetch Active Matchups (admin.php)** {#5.2.2.4-using-a-view-to-fetch-active-matchups-(admin.php)}

This retrieves matchup \+ vote data from a multi-join view and simplifies PHP logic. It is used for moderation and live status display. 

| `$query = $db->query("SELECT * FROM active_matchups_with_votes ORDER BY closes_at ASC"); $activeMatchups = $query->fetchAll(PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);` |
| :---- |

Loads all live matchups using a database view that handles complex JOIN logic. Simplifies PHP and supports live moderation.

#### **5.2.2.5 Executing Direct Queries (tournaments.php)** {#5.2.2.5-executing-direct-queries-(tournaments.php)}

Retrieving all tournaments via prepared statements: 

| `$stmt = $db->prepare("SELECT * FROM tournament ORDER BY start_at DESC"); $stmt->execute(); $tournaments = $stmt->fetchAll(PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);` |
| :---- |

Retrieves tournament lists for the main browsing page. 

#### **5.2.2.6 Calling get\_tournament\_stats (statistics.php)** {#5.2.2.6-calling-get_tournament_stats-(statistics.php)}

And, an example of how we display the results we get from the get\_tournament\_stats procedure from the statistics.php page is, the procedure returns distinct result sets (like overview, participation, top-entries, and vote distribution) in a single call. The PHP application layer handles this using nextRowset(), where we iterate through the result data effectively and deliver it without needing 4 separate database queries

| `$query = $db->prepare("CALL get_tournament_stats(:tid)");         $query->bindParam(":tid", $tournamentId, PDO::PARAM_INT);         $query->execute(); // RESULT SET: OVERVIEW         $overview = $query->fetchAll(PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);// RESULT SET: PARTICIPATION             $query->nextRowset();             $participation = $query->fetch(PDO::FETCH_ASSOC) ?: []; // RESULT SET: VOTE DISTRIBUTION             $query->nextRowset();             $roundStats = $query->fetchAll(PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);`  |
| :---- |

#### **5.2.2.7 Semantic Constraint Enforcement in PHP (cast\_vote.php)** {#5.2.2.7-semantic-constraint-enforcement-in-php-(cast_vote.php)}

Preventing double voting in the same matchup. Although the database has a Primary Key on (user\_id, matchup\_id) that effectively prevents double voting, relying solely on the database would result in a fatal SQL error. Instead, the application layer pre-checks if a vote exists. This allows us to provide a clean, user-friendly error message ("You have already voted") rather than crashing the script. 

| `// Check if user already voted on this matchup $voteCheck = $db->prepare(" SELECT COUNT(*) FROM vote     WHERE user_id = ? AND matchup_id = ?"); $voteCheck->execute([$userId, $matchupId]); $hasVoted = $voteCheck->fetchColumn(); if ($hasVoted) {     die("You've already voted in this matchup."); } // Insert the vote $insertVote = $db->prepare("     INSERT INTO vote (user_id, matchup_id, entry_id, cast_at)  VALUES (?, ?, ?, NOW())"); $insertVote->execute([$userId, $matchupId, $entryId]);` |
| :---- |

Implements rules that the database does not enforce on its own (e.g., early rejection before hitting DB constraints).

#### **5.2.2.8 Ensuring Matchup Status Before Voting**  {#5.2.2.8-ensuring-matchup-status-before-voting}

This constraint protects matchups from premature or late voting. 

| `if ($now < strtotime($matchup['opens_at']) || $now > strtotime($matchup['closes_at'])) {     die("This matchup is not currently open for voting."); }` |
| :---- |

Prevents premature or late voting and ensures voting windows align with tournament configuration. 

#### **5.2.2.9 Handling File Uploads for Profiles (edit\_profile.php)** {#5.2.2.9-handling-file-uploads-for-profiles-(edit_profile.php)}

Example of processing and storing user-uploaded images: 

| `if (!empty($_FILES['profile_picture']['name'])) {     $filename = uniqid() . "_" . basename($_FILES["profile_picture"]["name"]);     $target = "uploads/" . $filename;     if (move_uploaded_file($_FILES["profile_picture"]["tmp_name"], $target)) {         $stmt = $db->prepare("UPDATE users SET profile_picture=? WHERE user_id=?");         $stmt->execute([$filename, $user_id]);     } }` |
| :---- |

Processes image uploads, stores files on the server, and updates the user record with the image path.

#### **5.2.2.10 AJAX Constraint Enforcement (check\_displayname.php)** {#5.2.2.10-ajax-constraint-enforcement-(check_displayname.php)}

Real-time validation of display name availability:

| `$stmt = $db->prepare("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE displayname=?"); $stmt->execute([$displayname]); echo $stmt->fetchColumn();` |
| :---- |

Supports real-time validation on the client side to prevent duplicate display names before form submission. 

#### **5.2.2.11 Round Progression Polling (check\_round\_change.php)** {#5.2.2.11-round-progression-polling-(check_round_change.php)}

JavaScript on the client polls this PHP file periodically, and PHP returns the current tournament status. When the status changes, the GUI automatically updates the round display. 

| `$query = $db->prepare("     SELECT tourneystatus      FROM tournament      WHERE tournament_id = ? "); $query->execute([$tournament_id]); echo $query->fetchColumn();` |
| :---- |

This allows the front-end to detect status changes without page reloads. 

#### **5.2.2.12 Authentication Middleware** {#5.2.2.12-authentication-middleware}

To manage data flow and security, we implemented a reusable authentication layer in auth.php. Functions like ensure\_logged\_in() act as middleware, intercepting HTTP requests before they reach sensitive logic. If a user is not authenticated, the application layer halts execution and redirects them to the login page, preventing unauthorized access to database operations.

| `function is_guest() {     return (isset($_SESSION["role"]) && $_SESSION["role"] === "guest"); } function ensure_logged_in() {     // If not a real logged-in user, show the custom "denied" page     if (!isset($_SESSION["user_id"]) || is_guest()) {         // Optional: pass where they came from (e.g., stats) as a query param         header("Location: guest_denied.php?from=statistics");         exit;     } }`  |
| :---- |

#### **5.2.2.13 Server-Side API for Real-Time Check on Username** {#5.2.2.13-server-side-api-for-real-time-check-on-username}

To support the GUI's live validation features, the application layer exposes Web API endpoints. These PHP scripts accept asynchronous requests from the client (via AJAX) and query the database without reloading the page.

For example, check\_displayname.php accepts a username parameter, queries the users table to check for duplicates, and returns a simple text response ("taken" or "available"). This allows the application to enforce unique constraints before the user submits the form.

| `From the URL:https://artemis.cs.csub.edu/~fantasytourney/Final_project/check_displayname.php?displayname=` |
| :---- |

| `$db = get_pdo_connection(); $displayname = trim($_GET['displayname']); $user_id = isset($_GET['user_id']) ? intval($_GET['user_id']) : 0; // Query to check if name exists for another user $stmt = $db->prepare("     SELECT user_id      FROM users      WHERE LOWER(displayname) = LOWER(?)       AND user_id != ? "); $stmt->execute([$displayname, $user_id]); echo ($stmt->rowCount() > 0) ? "taken" : "available";`  |
| :---- |

### **5.2.3 \- Front-End Layer Programming** {#5.2.3---front-end-layer-programming}

The front-end layer is responsible for the user interface and client-side logic. Built using HTML, CSS, and Bootstrap, this layer ensures the application is responsive and interactive. We used JavaScript that runs in the user’s browser, handling client-side validation, AJAX polling, real-time validation, and dynamic interactive elements. Below are representative excerpts of the code used to support client-side behavior that connects to the PHP application layer. 

#### **5.2.3.1 HTML Structure for Round Voting (round8.php)** {#5.2.3.1-html-structure-for-round-voting-(round8.php)}

This HTML snippet shows how matchups are displayed and how voting buttons connect to PHP endpoints: 

| \<div class="matchup"\>     \<div class="entry"\>         \<img src="uploads/\<?= \$matchup\['entryA\_image'\] ?\>" class="entry-img"\>         \<p\>\<?= \$matchup\['entryA\_name'\] ?\>\</p\>         \<a href="cast\_vote.php?matchup=\<?= \$matchup\['matchup\_id'\] ?\>\&entry=\<?= \$matchup\['entryA\_id'\] ?\>"             class="btn btn-primary"\>Vote\</a\>     \</div\>     \<div class="entry"\>         \<img src="uploads/\<?= \$matchup\['entryB\_image'\] ?\>" class="entry-img"\>         \<p\>\<?= \$matchup\['entryB\_name'\] ?\>\</p\>         \<a href="cast\_vote.php?matchup=\<?= \$matchup\['matchup\_id'\] ?\>\&entry=\<?= \$matchup\['entryB\_id'\] ?\>"             class="btn btn-primary"\>Vote\</a\>     \</div\> \</div\> |
| :---- |

This defines how entries and voting buttons appear on the bracket screen. Buttons send GET requests to cast\_vote.php (the application layer).

#### **5.2.3.2 CSS Styling for Brackets (round8.css)** {#5.2.3.2-css-styling-for-brackets-(round8.css)}

This file controls the visual layout of the matchups, ensures uniform images and spacing, and applies the project’s color palette. 

| .entry-img {     width: 120px;     height: 120px;     object-fit: cover;     border-radius: 10px; } .matchup {     display: flex;     justify-content: space-around;     margin-bottom: 20px; } .btn-primary {     margin-top: 10px;     background-color: \#4A90E2;     border: none; } |
| :---- |

The most complex visual component is the Tournament Bracket. We created a custom CSS structure (round8.css) that uses Flexbox to align matchups into rounds (Round of 16 → Quarter Finals → Semi-Finals → Final). Pseudo-elements (:before, :after) are used to draw the connecting lines between matches dynamically.

| .tournament-headers {   flex-grow: 1;   display: flex;   flex-direction: row;   justify-content: space-around;   border-bottom: 1px solid \#ccc; } .tournament-brackets {   display: flex;   flex-direction: row;   list-style-type: none;   background: \#fdfdfd;   margin-bottom: 50px; } .bracket {   padding-left: 0;   display: flex;   margin: 0;   padding: 30px 0;   flex-grow: 1;   flex-direction: column;   justify-content: space-around;   list-style-type: none;   border-right: 1px dashed \#ccc;   flex: 1; } .team-item {   background-color: \#f4f4f4;   padding: 0.5rem;   display: block;   margin: 0.5rem 10px;   position: relative;   line-height: 2;   text-align: center; } .team-item:after {   content: '';   border-color: \#4f7a38;   border-width: 2px;   position: absolute;   display: block;   width: 10px;   right: \-11px; } .team-item:nth-of-type(odd):after {   border-right-style: solid;   border-top-style: solid;   height: 100%;   top: 50%; } .team-item:nth-of-type(even):after {   border-right-style: solid;   border-bottom-style: solid;   height: 100%;   top: \-50%; } .team-item:before {   content: '';   border-top: 2px solid \#4f7a38;   position: absolute;   height: 2px;   width: 10px;   left: \-10px;   top: 50%; }  |
| :---- |

#### **5.2.3.3 AJAX: Checking Display Name Availability**  {#5.2.3.3-ajax:-checking-display-name-availability}

To improve the user experience, we implemented AJAX requests using the JavaScript fetch() API. This allows the application to validate data and update the interface in real-time without reloading the page

On the Registration page (register.php, edit\_profile.php), an event listener detects keystrokes in the "Display Name" field. It sends an asynchronous request to the application layer to check availability. This provides immediate visual feedback (green tickmark/ red X) to the user.

| \<script\> function checkName() {     let name \= document.getElementById("displayname").value;     fetch("check\_displayname.php?name=" \+ name)         .then(response \=\> response.text())         .then(count \=\> {             if (count \> 0\) {                 document.getElementById("nameStatus").innerHTML \=                      "Display name already taken.";             } else {                 document.getElementById("nameStatus").innerHTML \=                      "Display name available.";             }         }); } \</script\> |
| :---- |

It sends an AJAX request to a PHP endpoint without reloading the page. Provides instant feedback to the user before submitting a form. 

#### **5.2.3.4 AJAX Round Status Polling** {#5.2.3.4-ajax-round-status-polling}

Uses JavaScript polling (setInterval) every 5 seconds. Calls a PHP endpoint that returns the current round/tournament status. If the status changes (round completed), the GUI refreshes automatically. Enables real-time bracket updates without user interaction. 

| \<script\> setInterval(() \=\> {     fetch("check\_round\_change.php?tournament\_id=\<?= \$tournament\_id ?\>")         .then(res \=\> res.text())         .then(status \=\> {             if (status \!== currentStatus) {                 location.reload();  // refresh UI automatically             }         }); }, 5000); \</script\> |
| :---- |

#### **5.2.3.5 Client-Side Form Validation (register.php)** {#5.2.3.5-client-side-form-validation-(register.php)}

Ensures basic input validation before submitting to the server. 

| \<script\> function validateForm() {     const email \= document.getElementById("email").value;     if (\!email.includes("@")) {         alert("Please enter a valid email.");         return false;     }     return true; } \</script\> |
| :---- |

Reduces invalid server requests.

#### **5.2.3.6 HTML Form Example (Profile Editing)** {#5.2.3.6-html-form-example-(profile-editing)}

Demonstrates how forms send data from the user to PHP scripts. 

| \<form action="update\_profile.php" method="POST" enctype="multipart/form-data"\>     \<label\>Display Name:\</label\>     \<input type="text" id="displayname" name="displayname" onkeyup="checkName()"\>     \<p id="nameStatus" class="text-muted"\>\</p\>     \<label\>Profile Picture:\</label\>     \<input type="file" name="profile\_picture"\>     \<button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary"\>Save Changes\</button\> \</form\> |
| :---- |

Links directly to AJAX validation. Supports file uploads to the server.

Dynamically generates HTML from PHP data. Displays analytics to players and admins.

#### **5.2.3.9 Interactive UI Elements (Tooltips)** {#5.2.3.9-interactive-ui-elements-(tooltips)}

We implemented dynamic tooltips using Bootstrap 5\. On the Tournament Bracket page (round8.php), we display the tournament creator's profile picture and username. Hovering over the username triggers a JavaScript-initialized tooltip that displays the creator's full bio. This was achieved by adding data-bs-toggle="tooltip" attributes to the HTML elements and initializing them via a global JavaScript function at the bottom of the page layout.

| `const tooltipTriggerList = document.querySelectorAll('[data-bs-toggle="tooltip"]')     const tooltipList = [...tooltipTriggerList].map(tooltipTriggerEl => new bootstrap.Tooltip(tooltipTriggerEl))`  |
| :---- |
